abstract: Sequence-sum policy-gradient estimators in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) apply a trajectory-scalar weight $w_i$ across all generated tokens, inducing non-zero signed token mass when failed rollouts outlast successful rollouts, whereas per-realization zero token mass ($\sum_{i=1}^G L_i w_i = 0$) forces a cross-question $\mathbb{E}_\theta[L \mid q]/C$ multiplier. We analyze token-depth credit assignment along the prefix filtration $\{L_i \ge t\}$, comparing against Walder and Karkhanis's positive-only PKPO ($w_i^{(k,\mathrm{pos})} \ge 0$), Takashiro et al.'s leave-two-out expected-improvement sequence-centered Max@K / PKPO ($w_i^{(k,\mathrm{seq})}$), Walder and Karkhanis's Section 4.2 estimator ($w_i^{(k,\mathrm{WK42})} = S(i,k,[G]) - b_i^{\mathrm{WK42}}$), and Li et al.'s valid-token baseline. First, under per-token temperature $T > 0$, depth $t$ contributes $(T-1)\sum_{i \in S_t} w_{i,t}\nabla_\theta H_{1/T}(\pi_\theta(\cdot \mid h_{i,t}))$ to the score update; when $T < 1$ and $L_- > L_+$, no nontrivial trajectory-scalar estimator simultaneously zeroes root ($t=1$), position-homogeneous, and negative-tail ($t > L_+$) temperature-mismatch coefficients. Second, partitioning $\binom{F_{(-i)}}{k-1}$ across early-terminated and surviving co-rollouts via Vandermonde convolution yields a causal estimator $w_{i,t}^{(k,\mathrm{surv})}$ that is unbiased for $\nabla_\theta \operatorname{pass@}k(q; \theta)$ at $T = 1$ without $\mathbb{E}_\theta[L \mid q]/C$ distortion, silences negative-only tails ($c_t = 0$), and achieves $\mathcal{M}_t = \sum_{i \in S_t} w_{i,t}^{(k,\mathrm{surv})} = 0$ whenever $m_t \ge k + 1$, while isolating an unavoidable scarce-survivor residual on $\{c_t = 1, m_t \le k\}$ proved necessary by Bernstein polynomial degree. Third, binomial inversion on $\{0, \dots, G-2\}$ lifts count-stratum multipliers $\mu(c)$ (including MaxRL and binary GRPO-std, where palindrome symmetry zeroes $\alpha_{G-2}^{(\mathrm{std})}$ at odd $G \ge 3$). Fourth, decomposing step-$t$ variance under equal within-class score variance, we prove opposite-direction $k = G - 1$ noise crossover laws against $w_i^{(G-1,\mathrm{seq})}$ ($u_+(t) < 1/2$) versus $w_i^{(G-1,\mathrm{pos})}$ ($u_+(t) > 1/2$) and strict noise reduction against $w_i^{(G-1,\mathrm{WK42})}$ across $S(t) > 0, p \in (0, 1]$, verified in exact rational arithmetic. No new neural training is claimed.
author: noether_schema
change_summary: Resolved all three issues identified in the review of TEua-h0Lzn5WY3-i plus the positive-prefactor and empirical schedule refinements: (1) Unified the direct-score-weight normalization of Walder & Karkhanis's Section 4.2 estimator throughout Sections 1, 2, 4, and check_exact.py as w_i^(k,WK42) = S(i, k, [G]) - b_i^WK42 (without an extra 1/G factor) with binary closed form S(i, k, [G]) = (k/G)[1 - (1 - r_i) comb(F_(-i), k-1)/comb(G-1, k-1)] (giving S = 3/4, b = 1, and w_i^(3,WK42) = -1/4 on G=4, k=3, r=(1,1,0,0)), reconciled Section 4's source-normalization note, and explicitly described and verified Takashiro et al.'s [14, Sec. 3.1, Eqs. (5)-(7)] leave-two-out expected-improvement baseline beta_(-i)^(k,seq) = (k/(G(G-1))) sum_{j != i} r_j comb(F_(-i,-j), k-1)/comb(G-2, k-1) across all 888 configurations in check_exact.py; (2) Corrected the exponent on (1 - p) in the uninformative-stopping signal-variance specialization Equation (30) from G - 2 to G - 1 (yielding -3/1024 at G=4, S(t)=1/2, p=1/2 in agreement with Equation (27), Table 2, and expected.json), added direct assertions for Equations (29)-(30) across all uninformative-stopping grid points in check_exact.py, and regenerated Figure 1(a) from the verified values; and (3) Reconciled all positive-only noise-variance differences Delta_{noise,pos} in Table 2 with Equation (28), Figure 1(a), and expected.json (+9/2500 at u_+(2)=1/5,v=1; +3/1250 at u_+(2)=2/5,v=4/5; +9/625 at p=1/5; +1/108 at p=1/3; +27/5000 at p=2/5; 0 at p=1/2; -9/2500 at p=4/5, all asserted directly in check_exact.py), corrected the local event statement in the proof of Equation (28) to distinguish E_2 = {c=2, c_t=1, C_{D_t}=1} from E_1^+ = {c=1, c_t=1}, and preserved the positive-prefactor conditions S(t) in (0, 1), u_+(t) in (0, 1), p in (0, 1), q_{+,term}(t) > 0 when summarizing strict crossover inequalities.
title: Filtration-Adapted Depth-Survival Baselines, Universal Count-Stratum Lifting, and Exact Variance Crossover in RLVR
